To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

water-filled cavities can be designed for high voltage gradient, high repetition rate, and CW operation; that the power losses in such cavities are small and can be reduced by proper design; and that the effects of beam loading on the cavity resonant frequency are not serious.

water-filled cavities can be designed for CW operation at 750 kV, 10 A, with a power efficiency of about 50 percent, and for pulsed operation at 750 keV, 1 kA with a pulse efficiency of about 80 percent.
water-filled RF cavities are a promising alternative for the acceleration of intense electron beams.

a water-filled RF accelerator that can produce a 1 kA electron beam at 750 kV with 10% efficiency and 10 Hz repetition rate.
the application of resonators to the generation and transport of high current, high energy electron beams.

the RF accelerator is a viable alternative to the linear induction accelerator.

the use of water in RF cavities offers a promising approach to the development of a high power RF accelerator for multi-kiloamp pulses and CW beams in the 10 to 50 A range.

the RF accelerator is a promising candidate for a high repetition rate, high average power, high efficiency, multi-kiloamp electron accelerator.
the RF cavity concept is a promising approach to the development of high current accelerators.
